description:
Have you ever under reported your smoking history, or left it out entirely, because you feared judgment or higher health insurance costs? You may think you’re protecting yourself, but withholding that information could mean risking your life.

Rebecca Mattson explores why people hesitate to share their full smoking history and why that conversation matters. She invites us to rethink what we tell our healthcare providers, and how we can make it easier for patients to speak openly, without shame.

An honest conversation could help protect your health, and save your life.

description:
Would you be able to work in a broken, toxic environment? Your immune cells face a similar challenge.

When immune cells fail, tumors can progress. But fixing the cells themselves doesn’t always work. Miguel Reina-Campos explores a different question: What if the problem isn’t just the cells, but the tissue structures they move through? Could redesigning that environment help immune cells do their job?
Learn more about Reina Lab: https://www.reinalab.org/

#CancerResearch #Immunotherapy #ImmuneCells #TEDx #TEDxSanDiego #MooresCancerCenter #Cancer #environment #health #research Dr. Miguel Reina-Campos is an Assistant Professor at La Jolla Institute for Immunology, where he leads the Laboratory of Tissue Immune Networks. His lab studies how immune cells live and function inside tissues, with the goal of improving long-term protection against infections and cancer. He uses advanced technologies to map immune cells in tissue environments and understand how their location shapes immune def

description: El 24 de marzo de 2023 una infección por estreptococo pyogenes la llevó a un shock séptico que casi le cuesta la vida. Lo que vino después, fue un camino de 500 días de internación, 50 cirugías y un proceso de rehabilitación en el que tuvo que reaprender a tragar, a escribir, a vestirse. Hoy Rochi está en silla de ruedas. Es una sobreviviente que decidió convertir esa experiencia límite en un mensaje de resiliencia con una autenticidad y fortaleza admirables recordándonos que incluso en los momentos más difíciles es posible encontrar esperanza, sentido y una nueva manera de vivir. Yoyo is one of the core members of the H-Infinity Social and Cultural Practice Programme ‘Once made in Hong Kong: Char Siu then and now’. She is currently pursuing a BSSc degree in the Department of Social Work, CUHK. Passionate about community development, local culture, and volunteerism, Yoyo actively collaborates with social enterprises to implement community projects. Her interests also extend to community building, intergenerational inclusion, and policy advocacy, through which she hopes to contribute to a more connected and compassionate society. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
In her talk , Kate challenges the idea that achievement defines our worth and explores why growth, curiosity, and effort matter far more than a score.

 Kate Ellen has spent years surrounded by numbers on papers and screens, digits that tried to tell her who she was and how much she was worth. For a while she believed them, celebrating every high score and feeling herself shrink with every lower one, until she realized that numbers can measure work but never identity. For her, they can’t capture curiosity, effort, courage, or the story behind each step forward. description: Arpan Talwar began his TEDx talk by introducing himself as the head of an organisation that supports cancer patients. He shared his personal journey of his wife being diagnosed with breast cancer while she was pregnant. In search of answers and possible treatments, he travelled to different cities and countries, but doctors told him that she might have only three to six months to live. He researched breast cancer, sought help from doctors, and established an organisation to support his efforts. Unfortunately, his wife passed away in March 2022, leaving him emotionally devastated and struggling with depression. Following this loss, he dedicated the next years of his life to researching about cancer, understanding its causes, and continuing his efforts to find answers about the disease and helping people. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Someone you love is going to say something that matters—and you're going to hear it and move on. We all do. We live fast, we triage, we tell ourselves we'll come back to it later. A trial lawyer shares two stories that shaped how he sees that moment: a 13-year-old boy a jury valued at $20 million, and a client whose quiet "I'm fine" he still thinks about years later. The lesson lands the same in every room—courtroom, kitchen, conference table. We don't miss what matters. We decide it doesn't. I’ve learned that if you want real justice for your clients, you can’t default to the easy path.
You take the big swings. You commit. You believe.
That mindset has defined my career.

I tried cases as a U.S. Army JAG Officer, as a Drug and Vice Prosecutor, and now as a partner at Gray Broughton Injury Law. 

There is nothing more professionally exciting to me than preparing for trial, and nothing more meaningful than standing up for people who put their trust in me.

Sharif graduated valedictoria
title: We Don’t Miss What Matters, We Decide What Doesn’t. | Sharif Gray | TEDxColumbiana

description:
Addiction isn't a loss of control—it's the opposite.
It's a perfectly functioning brain that learned the wrong map to safety, relief, and connection.
Dr. Jason Giles, an anesthesiologist, became addicted to fentanyl during his brutal residency. Through repetition, his brain built a powerful—but dangerous—pathway.
Recovery isn't about fixing a broken brain. It's about retraining a new one through consistent practice.
You are not broken. You are trained. And training can always be changed. Dr. Jason Giles, MD, is a triple board-certified physician in Addiction Medicine, Anesthesiology, and Pain Medicine. A graduate of UC Berkeley in molecular biology, he earned his medical degree from UC Davis, where he also completed his general surgery internship, anesthesiology residency with cardiac emphasis, and pain medicine training.
Early in his career, Dr. Giles served as a cardiac anesthesiologist and pain specialist, managing complex trauma, cardiac, and transplant cases. In 2005, he dedicate

Not all pain can be explained—and trying to fix it can keep us stuck. In this talk, Courtney Stasko challenges the belief that healing comes from answers. Instead, she shows how hope is created when we stop hiding our pain and start telling the truth, turning isolation into connection and connection into something powerful. Courtney Stasko is a storyteller, speaker, and founder of Starry is Hope, a nonprofit supporting families navigating grief after the loss of a military service member or first responder.

A scientist by training, she earned a BS from the University of Dayton and an MBA in Operations Management. She began her career in chemical manufacturing before becoming a recognized expert in healthcare supply chain sourcing
title: Hope Begins When We Stop Hiding the Darkness and Start Sharing It | Courtney Stasko | TEDxColumbiana
